features.name: Landing_Page
features.purpose: Introduces BWS4, explains that it and every example app were built using Spec4, and gives users a way to discover and open each available example app.

invocation.trigger: A user opens the application's home view.

inputs.name: example app listings
inputs.description: Name, short description, and entry point for each currently available example app.

outputs.primary: An overview view introducing BWS4 and a navigable list of example apps.
outputs.format: Text with a list of selectable entries
outputs.schema_notes: Each listed entry includes a name, a short description, and a way to open that example app.

success_criteria: A user unfamiliar with the project understands, within seconds, that BWS4 is a collection of example apps built with Spec4.
Every currently available example app appears in the list and can be opened.
The overall introduction and navigation remain reachable from any example app the user visits.

failure_modes.mode: A newly added example app fails to appear in the list
failure_modes.mitigation: The list is generated from a single shared source of truth for available apps rather than being maintained separately.

failure_modes.mode: Description text becomes stale relative to what an app actually does
failure_modes.mitigation: Each app's listing text is reviewed alongside its own educational overview.

features.name: RAG_Example_App
features.purpose: Demonstrates the retrieval-augmented generation pattern using a small, publicly available dataset, so a user can see how retrieved content shapes a generated answer.

invocation.trigger: A user opens the RAG example app and submits a question.

inputs.name: user question
inputs.description: A free-form question the user wants answered using the example dataset.

inputs.name: example dataset
inputs.description: A small, fixed, publicly sourced collection of passages the app retrieves from.

outputs.primary: An answer to the user's question along with the specific passages that were retrieved and used to produce it.
outputs.format: Text answer accompanied by a list of cited source passages
outputs.schema_notes: Each cited passage is distinguishable from the generated answer text.

success_criteria: Passages retrieved for a question are topically related to that question.
The generated answer visibly reflects and can be traced back to at least one retrieved passage.
A short educational explanation of the retrieval-augmented generation pattern is shown to the user.

failure_modes.mode: Retrieval returns passages unrelated to the question
failure_modes.mitigation: The example dataset is small and curated so relevant matches are likely; the app tells the user which passages were used so mismatches are visible.

failure_modes.mode: No passages match the question at all
failure_modes.mitigation: The app clearly informs the user that no relevant passage was found rather than fabricating a source.

features.name: Shared_Framework_Services
features.purpose: Provides the common capabilities every example app relies on — generating text with a model, producing embeddings, searching for information, and storing/retrieving small amounts of data — so each app doesn't need its own separate version.

invocation.trigger: An example app makes a request for generation, embedding, search, or data storage/retrieval while handling a user action.

inputs.name: capability request
inputs.description: An indication of which capability is needed (generate text, produce embedding, search, or store/retrieve data).

inputs.name: request payload
inputs.description: The content the capability should act on, such as a prompt, text to embed, a search query, or a record to store or fetch.

outputs.primary: A response appropriate to the requested capability.
outputs.format: Varies by capability: generated text, a numeric embedding representation, a list of search results, or a stored/retrieved record.
outputs.schema_notes: Every response is clearly tied to the capability that was requested.

success_criteria: Each capability returns a correct, usable response for valid requests from any example app.
Behavior of a given capability is consistent no matter which example app calls it.
The underlying model or provider behind a capability can be changed while the app keeps running, without interrupting users.

failure_modes.mode: The generation or search capability is temporarily unavailable
failure_modes.mitigation: The calling app receives a clear failure signal it can show to the user instead of an unexplained delay or blank result.

failure_modes.mode: Usage quota for a shared capability is exhausted
failure_modes.mitigation: Requests are limited per app and the user is informed clearly rather than receiving a silent failure.

failure_modes.mode: Different apps configure a shared capability inconsistently, causing divergent behavior
failure_modes.mitigation: Configuration for each capability lives in one shared place used by all apps.

features.name: Tool_Use_Integration
features.purpose: Gives example apps that need it the ability to look up current information from an external search capability as part of their reasoning, rather than relying only on a model's built-in knowledge.

invocation.trigger: An example app's workflow determines it needs to search for information to complete a step.

inputs.name: search query
inputs.description: The question or topic the app needs external information about.

inputs.name: surrounding context
inputs.description: Relevant context from the ongoing user request that helps focus the search.

outputs.primary: A list of search results relevant to the query.
outputs.schema_notes: Each result includes a short title, a snippet of relevant text, and a reference to its source.

success_criteria: Search results are topically relevant to the submitted query.
A calling example app can use the returned results to produce a more informed final answer.
The fact that a search was performed, and what was found, is visible and explainable to the end user.

failure_modes.mode: The external search capability is unavailable
failure_modes.mitigation: The calling app degrades gracefully and tells the user the search step failed rather than stalling.

failure_modes.mode: Search results are irrelevant to the query
failure_modes.mitigation: Results are shown to the user so relevance can be judged rather than hidden inside an opaque answer.
Usage is capped and the user is shown a clear message when the limit is hit.

features.name: Embeddings_Example_App
features.purpose: Illustrates the embedding pattern by visually plotting a curated set of texts in a two-dimensional space so users can see semantically similar items cluster together, and lets users add their own text to the same plot.

invocation.trigger: A user opens the Embeddings example app, and optionally submits custom text to add to the plot.

inputs.name: curated text examples
inputs.description: A predefined set of words, short phrases, and full sentences spanning a few categories, used to populate the initial plot.

inputs.name: custom text
inputs.description: Text the user enters to see embedded and placed alongside the curated examples.

outputs.primary: A two-dimensional visual plot of all embedded texts, with the user's custom entries visually distinguished from the curated ones.
outputs.format: Interactive visual chart with labeled points
outputs.schema_notes: Each point is labeled with its source text and marked as either a curated example or a user-added entry.

success_criteria: Curated examples belonging to the same category or meaning visibly cluster near each other in the plot.
When a user adds custom text, it appears merged into the same plot in a visually distinct way.
A short educational overview explains what an embedding is and why similar meanings cluster together.
The same shared embedding capability used elsewhere in the framework is used here, with no separate one introduced.

failure_modes.mode: Adding custom text causes the whole plot to shift unpredictably, confusing the user about what changed
failure_modes.mitigation: The plot is recomputed and redrawn clearly each time so the user can see the update happen rather than an unexplained jump.

failure_modes.mode: Custom text is unusual or nonsensical, producing a placement that seems arbitrary
failure_modes.mitigation: User-added points are clearly labeled as exploratory rather than authoritative.

failure_modes.mode: A very long custom entry causes a noticeable delay before the plot updates
failure_modes.mitigation: Guidance is given on a reasonable length for custom text.

features.name: Single_Call_Example_App
features.purpose: Demonstrates the single-call pattern — one direct prompt producing one direct response, with no retrieval or multi-step chaining — in both a plain-text mode and a structured-output mode.

invocation.trigger: A user opens the Single-Call example app and submits or selects a prompt, choosing a mode.

inputs.name: prompt text
inputs.description: A free-form prompt entered by the user.

inputs.name: preset prompt choice
inputs.description: One of a small set of ready-made example prompts the user can pick instead of writing their own.

inputs.name: mode
inputs.description: Whether the request should be handled as Simple (plain text) or Structured (schema-conforming response).

outputs.primary: The model's response to the submitted prompt.
outputs.format: Plain text in Simple mode; a structured response shown alongside the request that asked for it, in Structured mode.
outputs.schema_notes: In Structured mode, both the request that specified the expected response shape and the response itself are shown together.

success_criteria: Simple mode returns a coherent free-text answer to the submitted prompt.
Structured mode returns a response whose shape matches what was requested, and both the request and response are visible to the user.
Selecting a preset prompt fills in a usable prompt without further editing required.
A short educational overview explains the single-call pattern and when it is appropriate.

failure_modes.mode: Structured mode's response does not match the expected shape
failure_modes.mitigation: The mismatch is detected and clearly flagged to the user rather than silently displayed as if valid.

failure_modes.mode: An empty or excessively long prompt produces a degraded or unusable response
failure_modes.mitigation: Input guidance and a reasonable length limit are provided.

failure_modes.mode: The generation capability is temporarily unavailable
failure_modes.mitigation: A clear error is shown with no partial or misleading output.

features.name: Chained_Calls_Example_App
features.purpose: Demonstrates the chained-calls pattern by routing an initial request through exactly two sequential model calls, showing the user each call's role, its intermediate output, and the final output.

invocation.trigger: A user opens the Chained-Calls example app and submits an initial request.

inputs.name: initial request
inputs.description: The user's starting request that begins the two-step chain.

outputs.primary: The intermediate output produced by the first call and the final output produced by the second call.
outputs.schema_notes: Each block is labeled with the role of the call that produced it (e.g., first step vs. final step).

success_criteria: The output of the first call is visibly used as the input to the second call.
Both the intermediate and final outputs are displayed to the user, each clearly labeled by role.
The user is told upfront what each of the two calls is meant to do before submitting a request.
The user is told that this demo is limited to exactly two chained calls to conserve usage, and that the pattern itself supports any number of chained calls.
A short educational overview explains the chained-calls pattern.

failure_modes.mode: The second call fails after the first succeeds
failure_modes.mitigation: The intermediate output remains visible along with a clear notice that the final step failed.

failure_modes.mode: The user misunderstands what each call's role is meant to be
failure_modes.mitigation: Each call's role is described to the user before they submit their request.

failure_modes.mode: The shared usage limit is reached partway through the chain
failure_modes.mitigation: A clear message is shown when the limit is hit, with no partial or misleading final output presented.

nfr_goals: All example apps share a consistent layout and navigation so users can move between them without relearning the interface.
New example apps can be added and appear in navigation without disrupting existing apps or requiring users to notice any interruption.
Each example app's educational overview is understandable to a developer with no prior background in that specific pattern.
Typical interactions within an example app respond within a few seconds under normal conditions.
Shared capabilities (generation, embedding, search, storage) can be updated or swapped while the app keeps running, without interrupting users.
Overall usage stays within free-tier limits of underlying services so the collection of example apps remains sustainable for public, repeated use.
